criteria.format_with_table: A currency value is any ^[A-Z]{3}$ string; scales come from the pinned table, and table-missing codes fail at first monetary use, not at admission.
criteria.format_with_two: A currency value is any ^[A-Z]{3}$ string; table-missing codes silently behave as scale 2.
criteria.table_only: A currency value exists only for codes listed in the pinned ISO 4217 table; validation rejects everything else at the checking boundary.

currency_values.instructions: Which reading of the verified excerpts should govern currency values?

criteria.as_stored: Serialize each decimal at its stored scale, preserving trailing zeros and any negative-zero sign.
criteria.padded: Serialize each decimal with exactly 18 digits after the point.
criteria.unique: Serialize each decimal in the unique normalized form: no trailing fractional zeros, no point for integral values, 0 for zero.

decimal_strings.instructions: Which reading of the verified excerpts should govern canonical decimal strings?

criteria.compare_minor: Operators compare minor amounts and ignore currency, so 100 minor EUR equals 100 minor USD.
criteria.equal_decidable_ordered_strict: == and != return a boolean for unlike currencies (unequal unless identical value and unit); ordering operators fail for unlike currencies.
criteria.strict_everywhere: Every comparison operator, equality included, fails when the two currencies differ.

unlike_money.instructions: Which reading of the verified excerpts should govern unlike-currency comparison?

state: As CanLang lane-02 coordinator I need three readings of the attached verified excerpts, each choosing the alternative the excerpts best support.
